title: Pinakes egress + dialect policy
description: Pinakes's own answer to the KGP (`koine/specs/grounding-pack.md`) §7.2 egress question — may a record leave this project at all — and to the §5 dialect question — what logic a consumer of a Pinakes knowledge port is asked to evaluate. Koine holds the SHAPE of these two axes and nothing else (`koine/docs/self-describing-participant.md`, facet 3): the values below are Pinakes's instance data and live here, in the repo that emits them. No central component holds them, and no peer needs read access to this file — it is the source the served surfaces are checked against. The two axes are independent, and both are independent of the trust tier a row carries on its provenance (`contracts/trust-tier.ts`): egress says whether a record may cross a boundary, dialect says what a consumer may evaluate, trust says how much to believe it.
enforcedAtNote: The only conformant answer (KGP §7.2, koine ADR-0007 decision 5): a `local-only` record is filtered out in the emitting producer BEFORE any encoding — TSV, JSON, Neo4j, ProbLog or RDF-star — is written. Egress is not advisory metadata a consumer is trusted to honour, so a projection of a boundary-crossing pack can never contain `local-only` content.
dialectNote: Every knowledge port Pinakes publishes emits `grounding-only` (KGP §5) — reference facts about consensus reality, never evaluable runtime logic. This field is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for that claim: `contracts/capability-manifest.json` names this policy in `x_pinakes.egressPolicy` and `assertValidCapabilityManifest` rejects a port whose dialect is not this value, so a `horn-safe`/`full-prolog` port cannot be published without changing the policy first. `contracts/kgp.ts` reads the same field for its `DEFAULT_DIALECT`.

recordClasses.records: Canonical node and edge rows in the `contracts/canonical-schema.json` column contract, exported from `data/source/lexicons/*.tsv` as the csid-keyed TSV bundle under `build/corpus/`.
recordClasses.rationale: Reference data about the real world, admitted only under `licensePolicy` below — the corpus Pinakes exists to publish.

recordClasses.records: The KGP §2 entity-grounding pack — csid, entity type, aliases, reconciliation decision, the four provenance columns and the §7.1 licence manifest — in the content-addressed pack envelope.
recordClasses.rationale: The grounding surface a peer anchors its own ids against (KINP §6 names Pinakes the canonical authority for real-world entities). Per-relation egress inside a pack is decided by `relationEgress` below.

recordClasses.records: Contribution review-queue entries, community verifications, annotations and hypotheses — the operator/contributor working state behind `services/api/src/pinakes/routers/{contributions,annotations,community_verification,hypotheses}.py`.
recordClasses.rationale: In-flight curation state, not reference knowledge: a claim becomes exportable by being merged into a lexicon, not by sitting in the queue. `producedBy` is empty because no exporter reads it — the three exporters under `scripts/` read `data/source/lexicons/` and nothing else, which is what makes this class enforced rather than merely declared.

recordClasses.records: The rule-SFT / lore-QA SLM training records and every artifact of a KFT run over them — datasets, adapters, merged weights, GGUF exports.
recordClasses.rationale: `synthetic`/`proprietary`/`personal` tier, so the KFT (`koine/specs/fine-tuning.md`) §4.2 egress gate resolves every run LOCAL-ONLY and refuses a cross-boundary `compute.class` before any compute. This class is why the `finetune` capability advertises `x_specialization.egress: local-only`; `assertFinetuneCapability` reads the value from here rather than restating it.

relationEgress.note: Per-RELATION egress (which bridged predicates may cross, and towards whom) is carried per entry in the vendored koine registry mirror, not restated here — that document is generated from koine `registry/predicate-mapping.json` and re-vendored with `npm run regen:registry-mirror`. `scripts/export-insimul-pack.ts` (`assertSeedMappingsRegistered`) refuses to seed from an entry whose `egress` is not `exportable`, which is this policy's per-relation enforcement point. This block is a pointer, deliberately: two copies of a per-relation table is exactly the divergence the policy exists to prevent.

licensePolicy.note: The KGP §7.1 admission allowlist Pinakes releases under and admits on. `allowedSpdxClasses` is the SPDX-family filter the exporters actually apply (`DEFAULT_LICENSE_CLASSES` in `scripts/export-entity-grounding.ts`); `allowedClasses` is the same filter expressed in §7.1's class vocabulary, and `licensePolicyFor(allowedSpdxClasses)` in `contracts/kgp.ts` must reproduce it exactly — asserted by `egress-policy.test.ts`, so the two never drift. A record outside the allowlist is rejected with a report, never silently dropped.
